key_insight: ASTEROID teaches partially observed agents to explore by distilling a privileged expert’s actions on histories collected by the student itself.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a sample-efficient route to exploration policies for robotics and navigation, including vision-denied manipulation.
method: Collect on-policy interaction histories with a history-conditioned student under partial observability.
Use a privileged expert to label actions conditioned on the student’s collected context.
Train the student to search while uncertain and exploit once hidden task information is revealed.
evidence_signal: Across 11 environments, the abstract reports approximately 2× higher returns under fixed exploration budgets and 100× fewer interactions than RL baselines, plus a 40% success increase over standard distillation in real-world robot manipulation.
watch_item: Training requires a privileged expert capable of labeling student-visited contexts; obtaining such supervision may be difficult outside simulation.
paper_title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
